text.p: Spanish insurance group Mapfre said on Thursday its international expansion was near completion after the recent purchases of majority stakes in Venezuelan group La Seguridad and Peru's El Sol Nacional.
"In 1996 the phase of completing our international presence is over, particularly in Latin America," chief executive Manuel Martinez told journalists.
He said the only new acquisition planned was the purchase of a stake in El Salvador insurance firm La Centroamericana.
This deal should be done within two months, but Martinez declined to put a value or a percentage on the stake.
Beyond Spain, Mapfre's business is concentrated in Latin America, where it is present in more than 10 countries.
Investment in south and central America totals more than 40 billion pesetas, although the international division posted losses of 329 million pesetas in 1996.
But Mapfre expects a turnaround in 1997, with "substantial profits" of above 1.5 billion pesetas for that division.
"We expect our investments in Latin America to bear fruit from 1997," he said.
Last year, 32 percent of income was accounted by premiums from the international business.
Group consolidated income (including car insurance arm Mapfre Mutualidad and the stock-exchange listed Corporacion Mapfre) grew 11.6 percent to 603.58 billion pesetas.
